# 1 Load station locations for all sample collections (fish and macroinvertebrates)

Combine all station locations

```{r}

list.files(taxa.dir)

Fam.abund.station<-read.csv(paste0(taxa.dir, "/Macroinvert_MixedID_relative_abundance_rarified.csv")) |> dplyr::select(Original_ID, Latitude, Longitude, Agency) |> distinct() |> mutate(Taxa="Macroinvertebrates")

Fish.station<-read_xlsx(paste0(taxa.dir, "/Fish_relative_abundance.xlsx"))|> dplyr::select(Original_ID, Latitude, Longitude, Agency) |> distinct() |> mutate(Taxa="Fish")

#Combine all stations
#Note whether fish or invert (or both) is collected
Stations<-bind_rows(Fam.abund.station, Fish.station) |> distinct() |> 
  #format Original ID
  mutate(Original_ID=as.factor(as.character(Original_ID))) |> 
  #rounding coordinates to 5 decimal places to deal with slight differences in coordinate measurement; note: this should be done on original Fish/Invert abundance files to prevent confusion
  mutate(Latitude=round(Latitude, 5), Longitude=round(Longitude, 5)) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from=Taxa,  values_from = Taxa,       values_fn = ~ "yes",                        values_fill = "no") |> mutate(Both_taxa_collected=ifelse(Macroinvertebrates=="yes"&Fish=="yes", "yes", "no"))

#View(Stations)

```

# 2 Resolve Duplicate Stations

## Issue 1: Sites located in close proximity, part 1

-For duplicate site ID (duplicate 'Original_ID') - this appears to typically occur because site location was measured multiple times, during different site visits (*by the same agency*), have slightly different coordinate location values.

-Sites with duplicate IDs were checked manually via map. Duplicate sites that were sampled in the same location by the same agency (i.e., have the same 'Original_ID') but with slightly different coordinate locations were addressed by rounding Lat/Long values to 5 decimal places.

-Sites sampled in essentially the same location but by different agencies (or by the same agency but within 100m of each other) are addressed in part 2

```{r}


head(Stations)
names(Stations)
#View(Stations)

#First check for QC errors - 
#same site name, different coordinates

dup.site.ID<-Stations |> dplyr::select(Original_ID, Agency) |> janitor::get_dupes() |> distinct()
#View(dup.site.ID)

#25 remaining sites with exact duplicate names but slightly different Lat/Long
#All are EPA or Carver County

#Check these one by one: (note, mapped these in Arc GIS Pro for easier viewing)


#Convert stations to shape file

Stations_sf<-st_as_sf(Stations, coords=c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs=4269, remove=FALSE)


dup.site.ID$Original_ID


#For remaining duplicates, select one set of coordinates for each

#Remake Stations table, without pivoting
Stations<-bind_rows(Fam.abund.station, Fish.station) |> distinct() |> 
  #format Original ID
  mutate(Original_ID=as.factor(as.character(Original_ID))) |> 
  #rounding coordinates to 5 decimal places to deal with slight differences in coordinate measurement; note: this should be done on original Fish/Invert abundance files to prevent confusion
  mutate(Latitude=round(Latitude, 5), Longitude=round(Longitude, 5))


#View(Stations |> filter(Original_ID %in% dup.site.ID$Original_ID))


#For each individual site with a duplicate  location, replace all Lat/Longs with the first value in each group

Stations_corrected<-Stations |> group_by(Original_ID) |>  mutate(Latitude = first(Latitude), Longitude=first(Longitude)) %>%
  ungroup()

#View(Stations_corrected |> filter(Original_ID %in% dup.site.ID$Original_ID))

#Now recreate wide form of Stations!

Stations_corrected<-Stations_corrected |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from=Taxa,  values_from = Taxa,       values_fn = ~ "yes",                        values_fill = "no") |> mutate(Both_taxa_collected=ifelse(Macroinvertebrates=="yes"&Fish=="yes", "yes", "no"))

#View(Stations_corrected)

#Check for duplicates again!
dup.site.ID2<-Stations_corrected |> dplyr::select(Original_ID, Agency) |> janitor::get_dupes() |> distinct()
#no duplicates found! 
```

## Issue 2: Sites located in close proximity, part 2

Sites collected by different agencies in essentially the same spot (within 100m of each other). This script creates a new merged site ID for these sites, and selects one set of coordinates (Long/Lat) to use for them. It keeps all of the original site names in the combined name, and it tracks the original collecting agency. It also tracks whether at least one of the combined sites had fish and/or macroinvertebrates collected.

Note that this includes some sites (eg EC 3) that were sampled by the same agency, but in close proximity to each other (\<100m apart)

**Identify nearby pairs of sites (\< 100m apart):**

```{r}

#Convert Stations to spatial object, with a coordinate reference system that measures distance in meters

Stations_cor_sf<-st_as_sf(Stations_corrected, coords=c("Longitude", "Latitude"), remove=FALSE, crs=4269)

#project to USA Albers Equal Area Conic
Stations_proj<-st_transform(Stations_cor_sf, crs=5070)

#set buffer distance between points (in meters)
x_dist <- 100 

#Create a buffer of distance x around each point
buffered_points <- st_buffer(Stations_proj, dist = x_dist)

# Self-join to find which points fall within each other's buffers

neighbors <- st_join(Stations_proj, buffered_points |> dplyr::select(-c(Macroinvertebrates, Fish, Both_taxa_collected)), join = st_intersects, suffix = c("", "_neighbor"))

# Filter out self-matches (where index/ID is the same)
#ID pairs within 100m of each other
nearby_pairs <- neighbors %>% 
  filter(Original_ID != Original_ID_neighbor)

#View(nearby_pairs)

#188 sites within 100m of another site (but this includes matches in both directions)

#Note that in some cases there are >2 sites within 100m of each other (eg, BE 2)

#find combo name and order alphabetically in paste?

```

**Combine nearby pairs or groups of sites**

```{r}

#if station has a nearby neighbor, combine site ID names and agency designation, and select one of the lat/long coordinates


Stations_combined<-nearby_pairs |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  rowwise() |>
#Combine site ID for the sites in close proximity
  mutate(New_ID = map2(Original_ID, Original_ID_neighbor, ~
                        paste(sort(c(.x, .y)), collapse= '/'))) |> 
  mutate(New_ID=as.character(New_ID)) |> 
#Do the same for Agency
  mutate(Agency_combined=map2(Agency, Agency_neighbor, ~
                                paste(sort(c(.x, .y)), collapse= '/'))) |> 
    mutate(Agency_combined=as.character(Agency_combined)) |> 
#select only one set of coordinates for each combo
  group_by(New_ID) |> 
  mutate(Latitude = first(Latitude), Longitude=first(Longitude)) %>%
    ungroup() |> 
#now worry about sites that are in more than one pair
group_by(Original_ID) |> 
  mutate(Number_pairs=n()) |> 
  ungroup() 
  

#View(Stations_combined)

#One option for combining names - using igraph

#Separate paths into individual long rows to find overlaps

Stations_combined<-Stations_combined |> 
  mutate(id=1:nrow(Stations_combined))

Stations_combined_long <- Stations_combined %>%
  separate_longer_delim(New_ID, delim = "/")

#View(Stations_combined_long)

#Create a self-join to map elements that share the same row id
edges <- Stations_combined_long %>%
  inner_join(Stations_combined_long, by = "New_ID", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  select(from = id.x, to = id.y)

#View(edges)

#Turn these overlaps into a network graph and find "connected components"
library(igraph)
g <- graph_from_data_frame(edges, directed = FALSE)
clusters <- components(g)$membership

#Bring cluster groups back to the original data frame and combine strings
df_clusters <- data.frame(id = as.integer(names(clusters)), group_id = clusters)

#Summarize both New_ID and Agency ---
result <- Stations_combined %>%
  left_join(df_clusters, by = "id") %>%
  group_by(group_id) %>%
  summarise(
    # Combine, split, and unique-ify New_ID
    combined_path = paste(New_ID, collapse = "/") %>% 
      str_split("/") %>% 
      map_chr(~ paste(unique(.x), collapse = "/")),
    
    # Do exactly the same thing for the Agency column
    combined_agency = paste(Agency, collapse = "/") %>% 
      str_split("/") %>% 
      map_chr(~ paste(unique(.x), collapse = "/"))
  ) %>%
  select(-group_id)

View(result)

#Join combined_path back to the Original Dataset ---

#Expand the result so every single sub-ID in 'combined_path' gets its own lookup row
lookup_table <- result %>%
  mutate(lookup_ID = combined_path) %>% 
  separate_longer_delim(combined_path, delim = "/") %>%
  rename(Original_ID = combined_path) # Rename to match your original dataset column name

View(lookup_table)

#join back to your original dataset
final_joined_dataset <- Stations_corrected %>%
  left_join(lookup_table, by = "Original_ID")

# View the final dataset
View(final_joined_dataset)

#check on example where multiple sites where combined:
View(final_joined_dataset |> filter(str_detect(lookup_ID, "EC 3")))


#Replace coordinates for grouped sites with only one set of coordinates
#remove duplicates

Stations_final<-final_joined_dataset |> 
  mutate(SiteID=ifelse(is.na(lookup_ID), Original_ID, lookup_ID)) |> 
  mutate(Agency_original=Agency) |> 
  mutate(Agency_combined=ifelse(is.na(combined_agency), Agency, combined_agency)) |> 
  group_by(SiteID) |> 
#select one set of coordinates for each site group
    mutate(Latitude = first(Latitude), Longitude=first(Longitude)) %>%
#if Fish were collected at any site in a group and if Inverts were collected at any site in a group, set to yes, otherwise no?  
  mutate(Macroinvertebrates_combined = if_else(any(str_detect(Macroinvertebrates, "yes")), "yes", "no")) %>%
  mutate(Fish_combined = if_else(any(str_detect(Fish, "yes")), "yes", "no")) %>%
  ungroup()

View(Stations_final)
  
#check on example where multiple sites where combined:
View(Stations_final |> filter(str_detect(lookup_ID, "EC 3")))

  
#Clean up table
names(Stations_final)

Stations_final_clean<-Stations_final |> 
  dplyr::select(SiteID, Original_ID, Agency_combined, Agency_original, Latitude, Longitude, Macroinvertebrates_combined, Fish_combined) |> 
    dplyr::rename(Macroinvertebrates=Macroinvertebrates_combined, Fish=Fish_combined) |> 
    mutate(Both_taxa_collected=ifelse(Macroinvertebrates=="yes"&Fish=="yes", "yes", "no")) |> distinct()
  
View(Stations_final_clean)

View(Stations_final_clean |> filter(str_detect(SiteID, "EC 3")))


#Write cleaned Stations to file
write_xlsx(Stations_final_clean, paste0(env.dir, "/Stations_cleaned.xlsx"))
```

# 3 Link stations to NHD stream network

## 3.1 Convert sample locations to spatial object for mapping

```{r}

#Read in Station data so far
Stations_final_clean<-read_excel(paste0(env.dir, "/Stations_cleaned.xlsx"))

names(Stations_final_clean)

#Convert sample locations to spatial object:}

loc_sf<-st_as_sf(Stations_final_clean, coords=c("Longitude","Latitude"), crs=4269, remove=FALSE)

#View(loc_sf)

#Quick plot check of all compiled data:#(choose interactive or static viewing)

tmap_mode("view")

Sites.map<-
  tm_shape(loc_sf)+
  tm_dots()

Sites.map

#first transform to 
loc_proj <- st_transform(loc_sf, 5070) 

```

## 3.2 Get Area of Interest for extracting spatial attributes

```{r}

#Draw a bounding box around sample locations, for use in extracting hydrologic data

loc_bbox<-st_as_sfc(st_bbox(loc_sf))

plot(loc_bbox)

#Pull in HUC4 boundaries using nhdplusTools 
#These will be HUC4 boundaries that overlap with the study area bounding box 

HUC4<-get_huc(AOI = loc_bbox, type = "huc04") 

#plot locations of sample sites, and HUC4 boundaries  

tmap_mode("plot")  

tm_shape(HUC4)+   
  tm_borders(col="blue")+   
  tm_labels("name")+
tm_shape(loc_sf)+   
  tm_dots(fill="purple",fill_alpha=0.4)
  
  #tm_text("name", size = 1.0, col = "black", xmod = 0.2, ymod = -0.2, remove.overlap = FALSE)
```

Dissolve HUC4 boundaries to create a hydrologic AOI:

```{r}

HUC4_AOI <- st_union(HUC4)  

plot(HUC4_AOI)

tm_shape(HUC4)+   
  tm_borders(col="blue")+   
  tm_labels("name")+
  tm_shape(loc_sf)+   
  tm_dots(fill="purple",fill_alpha=0.4)+
  tm_shape(HUC4_AOI)+
  tm_borders(col="red")

st_crs(HUC4_AOI)

```

## 3.3 National Hydrography Dataset (NHD)

Use nhdplusTools package to link sample locations to NHD COMID (unique identifier for each stream reach of the NHD).

The COMID can then be used to link the location to NHD attributes (stream type, stream order, etc) as well as EPA StreamCat attributes.

To do this, we will join sample locations to NHD catchments. This avoids issues with sample location accuracy relative to flowlines (if you tried to join sample points to NHD flowlines rather than catchments).

\*\*Note that 'featureid' of an NHD Catchment is equal to COMID of an NHD flowline; see p. 47 of the NHDPlusV2 User Guide:

[https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2023-04/NHDPlusV2_User_Guide.pdf](https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2023-04/NHDPlusV2_User_Guide.pdf,)

### 3.3.a Download NHD catchment boundaries for area of interest

**Note: you only need to do this for your whole study area (the AOI) once**

Note: You need to use NHDPlusv2, as that is the NHD version with COMID identifiers that link to StreamCat. To encompass all Minnesota watersheds, NHDPlusv2 data is needed for the following regions:

09 Souris-Red-Rainy

07 Upper Mississippi

04 Great Lakes

10L Upper Missouri

10U Lower Missouri

#### Option 1: Download NHD data directly to GIS folder

Note: this is the method applied in the current approach.

Access via: <https://www.epa.gov/waterdata/get-nhdplus-national-hydrography-dataset-plus-data#Download>

Downloaded the catchment and NHD snapsot shapefiles from NHDPlusv2 for the above regions. Last accessed: 10.29.26. Catchment and NHD flowline shapefiles were merged and clipped to the bounding box surrounding all biomonitoring stations (which were first buffered to 1km), and exported as `NHDPlusv2_catchments_StationsBounded.shp`

```{r}

#read in NHD catchment layer for study area
#These were previously downloaded, merged and clipped into one shapefile in ArcGIS Pro

NHD_catchment<-st_read(paste0(spatial.dir, "/NHDPlusv2_catchments_StationsBounded.shp"))

#Create COMID column 

names(NHD_catchment)
NHD_catchment<-NHD_catchment |> 
  mutate(comid=FEATUREID)

```

```{r}
#Quick map check

tmap_mode("view")
tm_shape(NHD_catchment)+
  tm_borders()
```

#### Option 2: use nhdPlustools package

**NOTE: not needed if using Option 1 above**

Note, this can take considerable time for large spatial area, can sometimes crash, and sometimes fails to capture full spatial extent for large search area (i.e., large AOI).

Note that Feature ID= COMID for stream locations, see <https://www.epa.gov/national-aquatic-resource-surveys/streamcat-dataset-readme>

"StreamCat data is summarized for catchments, and in the catchment shapefiles, COMID is labeled as ‘FEATUREID’. Additionally, there is not a 1:1 relationship between stream segments and catchments - some stream segments have no corresponding catchment, and some sink catchments have no corresponding stream segments within them" - So this approach may not work for water bodies that aren't connected to stream network

```{r}

#Track how long it takes
Start.time<-Sys.time()  
Start.time

NHD_catchment<-get_nhdplus(
  AOI = HUC4_AOI,
  comid = NULL,   
  nwis = NULL,   
  realization = "catchment",   
  streamorder = NULL,   
  t_srs = NULL)  

End.time<-Sys.time()  

total.time<-End.time-Start.time
total.time 

st_crs(NHD_catchment)
names(NHD_catchment)  

#View(NHD_catchment)  

#Create COMID column 

NHD_catchment$comid<-NHD_catchment$featureid  

#Quick map check: 

tm_shape(NHD_catchment)+   
  tm_borders()  

#write to file if you want to save the stream network shapefile: 

#st_write(NHD_catchment, paste0(spatial.dir, "/nhd_catchment_R.shp"), append=FALSE)

```

### 3.3.b Identify NHD COMIDs associated with sample locations

see NHDv2Plus User Guide: <https://nhdplus.com/NHDPlus/NHDPlusV2_documentation.php>

```{r}


#transform sample points and catchments to same projection:  

#continental US (Conus Albers NAD83)    

loc_proj <- st_transform(loc_sf, 5070) 

NHD_catch_proj<-st_transform(NHD_catchment, 5070)
names(NHD_catch_proj)

#Join catchment attributes to sample locations:

loc_NHD <- st_join(loc_proj, NHD_catch_proj %>% dplyr::select(comid, AreaSqKM), join = st_intersects)    

View(loc_NHD)

#Check for NA values in comid
loc_NHD |> filter(is.na(comid))

#Check sites with NA for COMID

tm_shape(loc_NHD)+
  tm_dots()+
tm_shape(loc_NHD |> filter(is.na(comid)))+
  tm_dots(fill="red")

#1 site excluded, which does not overlap with NHDPlusV2, is in a Canadian watershed

#write to file (without geometry)

write_xlsx(loc_NHD %>% st_drop_geometry(), paste0(env.dir, "/Stations_clean_comid.xlsx"))
```

## 3.4 Sites within the same NHD catchment

For multiple sites within the same comid (the same NHD catchment), but with distinct locations (i.e., longitudinally along a river reach)

-For analysis, one option is to group the samples by comid, and treat them as repeat visits. –\> use the COMID as the site ID!

-An issue: sometimes real information is tracked in these close sites within the same comid- ie, up and downstream of changes in topography, elevation, land use, inputs, etc (might be quite specific). For example Riley Creek or Battle Creek sites. Combining them might be OK for most watershed scale effects, but may need to track variability in outcomes.

-Possible ways to handle this for spatial analysis across catchments:

-pick site closest to catchment outlet

-have some estimate of catchment variability

-One thing that could help is to track how many catchments have multiple sites longitudinally (for this to be most useful, probably do want to combine sites within 100m of each other)

**Identify if sites are part of a longitudinal series in a catchment**

(i.e., \> 1 site per NHD catchment)

```{r}

#read in Stations data so far

Stations_clean_comid<-read_excel(paste0(env.dir, "/Stations_clean_comid.xlsx"))

names(Stations_clean_comid)

Stations_clean_comid<-Stations_clean_comid |> 
  group_by(comid) |> 
  mutate(Num_sites_catchment=n()) |> 
  ungroup()

View(Stations_clean_comid)

#Look at breakdown for # of sites per NHD catchment

summary(Stations_clean_comid$Num_sites_catchment)

#Most sites have 1 sample per catchment, but a minority have more

Stations_clean_comid |> dplyr::select(Num_sites_catchment) |> group_by(Num_sites_catchment) |> count()

#update Stations file
write_xlsx(Stations_clean_comid, paste0(env.dir, "/Stations_clean_comid.xlsx"))

```

## 3.5 Identify sites closest to NHD catchment outlet

NOTE: UNDER CONSTRUCTION 11.9.26 - this section not yet complete

(i.e., most downstream site in any catchment)

```{r}

# 1. Load spatial locations (if not already loaded)
Stations_clean_comid<-read_excel(paste0(env.dir, "/Stations_clean_comid.xlsx"))

#Convert to shape file
Stations_clean_sf<-st_as_sf(Stations_clean_comid, coords=c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs=4269)

#Project stations
Stations_clean_proj<-st_transform(Stations_clean_sf, crs=5070)

#Load NHD stream network (downloaded in section 3.3):
nhd_flowline <- st_read(paste0(spatial.dir, "/NHDFlowline_merge_StationsBounded.shp"))

#Project flowlines to same crs
nhd_flowline_proj<-st_transform(nhd_flowline, crs=5070)

names(nhd_flowline_proj)

# 2. Find nearest feature index and compute the nearest point on the line
nearest_idx <- st_nearest_feature(Stations_clean_proj, nhd_flowline_proj)
nearest_lines <- nhd_flowline_proj[nearest_idx, ]

# 3. Project points onto the lines
snapped_points <- st_line_project(nearest_lines, Stations_clean_proj)

#Snap points to the closest NHD flowlines to find reach measures (i.e., distance along the flowline)
# This function calculates where the point snaps along the reach

start.time<-Sys.time()
start.time

#try downloading nhd using nhdplustools (note that this may not work for large areas)

indexed_points <- get_flowline_index(
  flines = "download_nhdplusv2",
  points = Stations_clean_proj,
  search_radius = 100,
  max_matches=1)

#Note - need to check to see whether this is pulling info for correct line, if point is close to two lines

end.time<-Sys.time()
end.time

# 3. Combine your original point data with the NHD indexing attributes
points_with_nhd <- bind_cols(my_points, indexed_points)

# 4. Group by Catchment (COMID) and pick the point closest to 0 (most downstream)
most_downstream_points <- points_with_nhd %>%
  group_by(COMID) %>%
  slice_min(order_by = REACH_MEAS, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()
```

# 4. Important! Add clean station info to Fish and Invert datasets!

The final selected coordinates for each site ID will also need to be assigned to the final Fish and Invert relative abundance files, and rewriting those final files (see below).

NOTE: check for "repeat" visits on same date and site ID combo, that might be data sources originally merged from multiple sources OR slightly different samples that could be treated as replicates (eg, EC3)

-EC3 is particularly tricky, because upstream and downstream sites were sampled on the same day; so if you combine IDs, these will basically become replicates - are you going need to reaggregate abundance by site/date once IDs are combined? or assign replicates

-\*\*Check for this! How many "replicates" does this create? Is there a way to track this? (if you keep track of their original IDs, that could be way to track replicates on same date)

## 4.1 Combine sites into groups and recalculate relative abundance of sites in a group were sampled on the same date

```{r}

#Read in cleaned up Stations file:

Stations_clean_comid<-read_excel(paste0(env.dir, "/Stations_clean_comid.xlsx"))

#Read in fish/invert datasets

list.files(taxa.dir)

#--------------------------------------------
#Macroinvert dataset: FAMILY ID
#--------------------------------------------
invert_Family<-fread(paste0(taxa.dir, "/Macroinvert_Family_relative_abundance_rarified.csv"))

names(invert_Family)

View(invert_Family)
#if Original station IDs are within combined name in Station file, combine
#If samples were collected on same day from multiple sites, recalculate relative abundance
#and replace Lat/Long with coordinbates for combined site

names(Stations_clean_comid)
View(Stations_clean_comid)

#if same merged name and same date but different Original ID, treat as replicates and combine counts

invert_Family2<-invert_Family |>
  dplyr::select(-c(Latitude, Longitude)) |> 
#add new combined SiteID where appropriate, keep Lat/Long from new merged ID
  left_join(Stations_clean_comid, by=c("Original_ID")) |> 
  #if samples collected from combined site ID on same day, recalculate relative abundance (this should be a very rare occurrence, but just in case)
  #note that suborder is excluded here, as some lumped families cross different suborders;
  group_by(SiteID, Date, Year, Agency_combined, Latitude, Longitude, phylum, class, order, family) |> 
  dplyr::summarize(Fam_sitegroup=sum(FamRarifyCount)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  group_by(SiteID, Date) |> 
  mutate(Total_fam_ALL_specimens_rarifed=sum(Fam_sitegroup)) |> 
  mutate(Rel_abund_fam=Fam_sitegroup/Total_fam_ALL_specimens_rarifed) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  rename(FamRarifyCount=Fam_sitegroup) |> 
  #put columns in more legible order
```

## 4.2 Add a flag for sites that were sampled over adjacent days (indicating these samples could be combined)

```{r}

#For Fish

Fish2_flagged <- Fish2 %>%
  #group by SiteID
  group_by(SiteID) %>%
  #make sure Date is formatted as Date
  mutate(Date=as.Date(Date)) |>
  #arrange dates in order for each site
  arrange(Date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
 #calculate lag time between each set of rows
  mutate(
    diff_prev = (Date - lag((Date))),
    diff_next = (lead(Date) - Date)
    #Adjacent_day_collection = (diff_prev = 1 | diff_next = 1
    ) %>%
  mutate(Adjacent_day_collection=ifelse(diff_prev=="1 days"|diff_next=="1 days", "Yes", "No")) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  #if any rows in a site/date combo are one, mark Adjacent_day_column as yes
  group_by(SiteID, Date) |> 
  mutate(
    Adjacent_date_sampled = if_else(any(c(diff_prev, diff_next) == 1, na.rm = TRUE), "yes", "no")
  ) |> 
  ungroup()

View(Fish2_flagged)

View(Fish2_flagged |> filter(Adjacent_date_sampled=="yes"))

View(Fish2_flagged |> filter(str_detect(SiteID, "USGS-05086000")) |> 
       filter(Year=="1994")
     
)

#Some samples collected over two days, some over 3

#Option to recalculate relative abundance across two adjacent days
#An imperfect solution could be to group by SiteID and Year, and recalculate relative abundance
#Only issue is if for some reason a site was sampled twice in one year at different times in the summer
#You can inspect manually if this is the case - it isn't for fish as of 11.12.26

#First make look up table to match the first date of each collection to the site/year group
Date.match<-Fish2_flagged |> 
  filter(Adjacent_date_sampled=="yes") |> 
  dplyr::select(SiteID, Date, Year) |> 
  distinct() |> 
  group_by(SiteID, Year) |> 
  slice_head(n=1)
Date.match

Fish2_flagged_grouped<-Fish2_flagged |> 
#only for samples with adjacent day collections
    filter(Adjacent_date_sampled=="yes") |> 
  #recalculate abundance by Year, leave out date for now
  group_by(SiteID, Latitude, Longitude, Agency_combined, Year, Genus, Species, FullScientificName, CommonName) |>
  #first recount number of each species by site group & date
  summarize(Number_adjacentday=sum(Number)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  
  #then recalculate relative abundance by site/year
  group_by(SiteID, Year) |> 
  mutate(TotalCount=sum(Number_adjacentday)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(Relative_abundance=Number_adjacentday/TotalCount) |>
  #Rename number column
  mutate(Number=Number_adjacentday) |>
  #add first day of collection back in as date
  left_join(Date.match, by=c("SiteID", "Year")) |> 
  #put columns in more legible order
  dplyr::select(SiteID, Date, Year, Latitude, Longitude, Agency_combined, Genus, Species, FullScientificName, CommonName, Number, TotalCount, Relative_abundance)

#Spot check that this worked correctly:

View(Fish2_flagged_grouped)

View(Fish2 |> filter(str_detect(SiteID, "USGS-05086000")) |> 
       filter(Year=="1994"))
```

# 5 Link to EPA StreamCat Attributes

## 5.1 Get StreamCat attributes using StreamCatTools

Note: These attributes are pulled for the state of MN, so unless new attributes are added/selected, you should only have to run this section once, to generate attributes for all comids in MN.

The `StreamCatTools` package was designed to simplify the use of [StreamCat](https://www.epa.gov/national-aquatic-resource-surveys/streamcat-dataset) data in R, leveraging the new [API for StreamCat](https://api.epa.gov/StreamCat/streams/metrics).

There are different ways to request data: by area of interest, by state, or by a list of COMIDs.

Note 1: StreamCat attributes apply to two different scales: 1) catchment scale (called 'Cat') and 2) watershed scales (called 'Ws'). Each attribute will have 'Cat' or 'Ws' in the column name depending on which scale it applies to.

StreamCat Variable list can be seen here (however, note that not all the variables in the streamcat list are in this explainer variable list): <https://www.epa.gov/national-aquatic-resource-surveys/streamcat-metrics-and-definitions>

Some additional metadata on new Streamcat attributes: <https://pasteur.epa.gov/uploads/10.23719/1532282/documents/StreamCatNNI_readme.txt>

Note: To access StreamCat data for a large number of sites, the most successful strategy appears to be to pull them by state. If you try to pull by long list of comids, you often get a bad request error. But, pulling by state can take considerable time (1-2 hours).

```{r}


#Note - pulling StreamCat attributes using StreamCatTools seems to function better in the morning hours; afternoon is more likely to see a 502 bad gateway error (maybe based on broader traffic etc)

#Get a list of all Streamcat attributes available: 
All.Streamcat<-sc_get_params(param="metric_names")
All.Streamcat

#View(as.data.frame(All.Streamcat))

#Get all variable descriptions!!
Definitions<-sc_get_params(param='variable_info')
#View(Definitions)

#Subset the Streamcat attributes you want to use
#eliminate fire related, containing "burn", "sev", "fire", "procmask"
#remove veg change, "vegresp", forest loss "frstloss"
#select relevant NLCD year & eliminate all other years
#the following attributes are all based on NANI and are available every year, retain one of each variable for the year of interest, exclude all others: "n_ff, p_ff, n_uf,p_uf,p_hw,n_hw,n_lw,p_lw,n_cr,p_cr,n_cf,n_lwr,p_lwr,n_ags,p_ags"

All.Streamcat<-as.data.frame(All.Streamcat)


#Clean up metrics filtering logic (fix vector reference in dplyr)
Streamcat.select <- All.Streamcat %>% 
  filter(!grepl('burn|sev|fire|procmask', All.Streamcat)) #%>% 
  #filter(!grepl('2001|2004|2006|2008|2013|2016|2019', All.Streamcat)) %>% 
  #filter(!grepl('_19|_20', All.Streamcat))

metrics_vec <- Streamcat.select$All.Streamcat

#Or for all metrics
#metrics_vsc<-All.Streamcat$All.Streamcat

#Pull metrics sequentially or in small groups, otherwise will hit bad gateway error  

metric_chunks <- split(metrics_vec, ceiling(seq_along(metrics_vec) / 5))

#-----------------------------------------------------------
#Get cat and ws scale metrics
#-----------------------------------------------------------

#Check time
start.time<-Sys.time()
start.time
# Loop over metric chunks instead of sending all at once
sc_data_list <- lapply(metric_chunks, function(m_chunk) {
  m_list <- paste0(m_chunk, collapse = ",")
  
  # Fetch data across COMIDs for this metric subset
  # Using county or state parameter if fetching all COMIDs in Illinois
  tryCatch({
    sc_get_data(
      metric = m_list, 
      aoi = "cat,ws", 
      state = "MN", # Direct state fetch if fetching all of Minnesota
      showAreaSqKm = FALSE
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Failed chunk: ", e$message)
    return(NULL)
  })
})

# Merge columns across results
sc_data <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = "comid", all = TRUE), sc_data_list)

View(sc_data)

#Write to file to save intermediate work
fwrite(sc_data, paste0(env.dir, "/Streamcat_MNBIO_cat_ws.csv"))

#------------------------------------------------------------
#Run again for riparian attributes
#-----------------------------------------------------------

# Fetch data across COMIDs for this metric subset
# Using county or state parameter if fetching all COMIDs in Illinois
start.time<-Sys.time()
start.time
sc_data_list <- lapply(metric_chunks, function(m_chunk) {
  m_list <- paste0(m_chunk, collapse = ",")
  
  tryCatch({
    sc_get_data(
      metric = m_list, 
      aoi = "catrp100,wsrp100", 
      state = "MN", # Direct state fetch if fetching all of Minnesota
      showAreaSqKm = FALSE
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Failed chunk: ", e$message)
    return(NULL)
  })
})

# Merge columns across results
sc_data_rp <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = "comid", all = TRUE), sc_data_list)

end.time<-Sys.time()
end.time

end.time-start.time 
#Write to file to save intermediate work
fwrite(sc_data_rp, paste0(env.dir, "/Streamcat_MNBIO_catRP_wsRP.csv"))


```

## 5.2 Merge StreamCat attributes by COMID to sampling location

Note: if you merge all attributes to all water quality data, it creates a very large dataset that is slow to work with. So if you need something that is quicker to work with, you may want to subset attributes or water quality data you want first before merging them.

Something else important to know! StreamCat summarizes attributes at both the watershed ("ws") and catchment ("cat") scale. watershed is all the land area draining into a stream reach, catchment is just the local land and does not include all the upstream areas.

```{r}


#Read in Station data
Stations_clean_comid<-read_excel(paste0(env.dir, "/Stations_clean_comid.xlsx"))

#Read in StreamCat data for all MN sites

sc_data<-fread(paste0(env.dir, "/Streamcat_MNBIO_cat_ws.csv"))

sc_data_rp<-fread(paste0(env.dir, "/Streamcat_MNBIO_catRP_wsRP.csv"))

#Merge to sample points

#first cat, ws: 
BIO.streamcat<-left_join(Stations_clean_comid, sc_data, by="comid")

head(BIO.streamcat)

#then catrp100, wsrp100

BIO.streamcat.all<-left_join(BIO.streamcat, sc_data_rp, by="comid")

names(BIO.streamcat.all)

View(BIO.streamcat.all)


#Check for loss of stations
nrow(Stations_clean_comid)
nrow(BIO.streamcat.all)

#Write to file to save intermediate work (use fwrite for large file, much faster than write.csv)
fwrite(BIO.streamcat.all, paste0(env.dir, "/Streamcat.MNBIO.all.csv"))
```

# 6 Explore Environmental Data

## 6.1 Examine change in riparian and watershed scale land use

Note: is there a better dataset to use for this?

```{r}

#Load StreamCat data 

sites.streamcat<-fread(paste0(env.dir, "/StreamCat.MNBIO.all.csv"))

head(sites.streamcat)
nrow(sites.streamcat)

tot.num.sites<-nrow(sites.streamcat)




View(sites.streamcat)

#For a given variable, extract year and add as column?
#a pivot_longer, with Year as a column

names(sites.streamcat)

cover.long<-sites.streamcat %>% dplyr::select(matches("decid|mxfst|conif|wet|Original_ID|Longitude|Latitude|catarea|wsarea|comid")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = contains(c("decid", "mxfst", "conif", "wet")),
    names_to = "Landcover",
    values_to = "Pct"
  ) %>% 
  #extract  year
   mutate(Year = as.integer(str_extract(Landcover, "\\d{4}"))) %>% 
  #remove year from landcover class
  mutate(Landcover = str_remove(Landcover, "\\d{4}")) 

summary(cover.long$Year)

#Calculate change in land cover between years, 2001-2019
change<-cover.long %>% 
 group_by(Original_ID,Landcover) %>%
#Arrange by year to ensure correct math
  arrange(Year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
#Calculate the difference from the previous year
  mutate(Pct_diff = Pct - lag(Pct)) %>% 
  ungroup()

View(change)
names(change)


#Mean difference between measured years acros sites

change %>% 
  filter(!is.na(Pct_diff)&grepl("rp", Landcover)) %>% 
  group_by(Landcover) %>% 
  summarise(mean=mean(Pct_diff), median=median(Pct_diff), min=min(Pct_diff), max=max(Pct_diff), na.rm=TRUE)

#Very small changes in mean riparian cover, when viewed across all sites

#There have been changes on a site by site basis, but the changes somewhat balance out across all sites 

#Sites with a non-zero change?
change %>% filter(abs(Pct_diff)>5) %>% dplyr::select(Original_ID) %>% distinct()


#Sum all changes by site

Tot.Diff<-change %>% filter(!is.na(Pct_diff)) %>% group_by(Original_ID, comid, Landcover) %>% 
  summarise(total_pct_diff=sum(Pct_diff)) %>% ungroup()
View(Tot.Diff)

#Mean total change across sites 
View(Tot.Diff %>% 
  filter(!is.na(total_pct_diff)&grepl("rp", Landcover)) %>% 
  group_by(Landcover) %>% 
  summarise(mean=round(mean(total_pct_diff),2), median=median(total_pct_diff), min=min(total_pct_diff), max=max(total_pct_diff)) %>% 
  #watershed scale only
  filter(grepl("ws", Landcover)))

#A small mean decrease in riparian conifer and mixed forest cover across sites, a small increase in deciduous forest cover
#But note that there are some sites that have quite large differences

#Sites with a non-zero change?
View(Tot.Diff %>% 
  dplyr::select(matches("rp|total_pct_diff|Landcover|Original_ID")) %>% 
  filter(abs(total_pct_diff)>1) %>% 
  dplyr::select(Original_ID) %>%
    distinct())

#305 sites have at least 5% total change in one riparian forest land use category over the total time period
#1482 sites have at least 1% total change in one riparian forest land use category over the total time period; (31% of sites)

305/tot.num.sites
1482/tot.num.sites


levels(factor(Tot.Diff$Landcover))

#Plot Histogram of Total Change?
#bindwith of 1 would be equal to 1 percent change

ggplot(Tot.Diff %>% filter(grepl("rp", Landcover)) %>% filter(grepl("cat", Landcover)))+
  geom_histogram(aes(total_pct_diff), binwidth=1, colour = "black", fill ="steelblue")+
  facet_wrap(~Landcover)+
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "white", linewidth = 0.5)+
  theme(panel.grid=element_blank())


#Majority of sites show =<1% change over the total period, for all kinds of forest

```

```{r}
catchment_landcover_wide<-catchment_landcover_wide %>% mutate(`% conifer riparian`=pctconifwsrp100, `% deciduous forest riparian` =pctdecidwsrp100, `% mixed forest riparian`=pctmxfstwsrp100, `% woody wetland riparian`=pctwdwetwsrp100, `% herb wetland riparian`=pcthbwetwsrp100)

names(catchment_landcover_wide)

LU.map<-tm_shape(catchment_landcover_wide) +
    tm_polygons(
        fill = c(
          #"pctconifws", 
          "% conifer riparian", 
          #"pctdecidws", 
          "% deciduous forest riparian", 
          #"pctmxfstws", 
          "% mixed forest riparian", 
          #"pctwdwetws", 
          "% woody wetland riparian",
          "% herb wetland riparian"),
#make polygon borderes transparent!
        col_alpha = 0,
        fill.free=FALSE,
        fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(breaks=c(-30,-15,-5, -1,0,1,5,15, 30),
            values = palette2),
fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Change in % land use")
    )+
tm_layout(
    bg.color = "white")+
#option for vertical stacking:
#tm_facets_vstack()
tm_facets(ncol=3)

LU.map

#################################
#Method 2 (long data):
tm_shape(catchment_landcover %>% filter(!is.na(Landcover))) +
    tm_polygons(
        fill = "total_pct_diff",
        #col = NA,
        lwd=0,
        col="white",
        fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
            values = palette
        )
    )+
  tm_facets_stack()
```

For sites with temporal change in forest cover, what is coverage of biomonitoring data?

```{r}

#Subset to sites with 5% or more change in riparian land use
Sites.with.change<-(Tot.Diff %>% 
  dplyr::select(matches("rp|total_pct_diff|Landcover|Original_ID")) %>% 
  filter(abs(total_pct_diff)>=5) %>% 
  dplyr::select(Original_ID) %>%
    distinct())

Sites.with.change

#Subset macroinvert data to these sites
Sites.subset<-Fam.abund %>% 
  filter(Original_ID %in% Sites.with.change$Original_ID)

#How many visits and year range for each site?

View(Sites.subset %>% 
  dplyr::select(Original_ID, Date) %>% distinct() %>% 
 group_by(Original_ID) %>%
  summarise(
    total_dates = n(),
    start_date  = year(min(Date, na.rm = TRUE)),
    end_date    = year(max(Date, na.rm = TRUE))
  ) %>% 
   filter(total_dates>1))
  
#120 with changing riparian land use (>5%) sites visited more than once
#1996-2024
```
